ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T1_CONVERSATIONAL_SKILL.I.mastery: Chooses the polite way to introduce yourself, a friend or a visitor (May I introduce my friend, Wanjiru? Pleased to meet you), puts the person of honour first, and spots a rude or blunt turn, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the book for a purpose
judge the relevance of a text
ENGL.G7.READIN.T1_EXTENSIVE_READING_IN.S.mastery: Chooses the book or text that fits what the reader needs (information, enjoyment, a topic, a level), tells fiction from non-fiction, and does not choose by the cover, the length or the title alone, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.NOU.mastery: Names a noun as common (river), proper (Mombasa), collective (a flock of birds) or abstract (courage), picks the collective noun that goes with a group (a swarm of bees), and writes a capital letter for a proper noun only, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the trick or the lesson
choose what the trickster is like
ENGL.G7.READIN.T1_INTENSIVE_READING_TR.T.mastery: Says that a trickster is a clever character who gets what it wants by a trick (Hare, Spider), names the trick and who is fooled, and says what the story teaches, and does not call the trickster a hero or the fooled one a trickster, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T1_HANDWRITING_LEGIBILI.H.mastery: Names the features of neat handwriting (letters of an even size that sit on the line, tall and short letters kept distinct, clear spaces between words, a steady slant) and says why it matters, and does not take fast, decorated or crowded writing for neat, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the best way to tell this part
ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T2_ORAL_PRESENTATIONS_O.O.mastery: Names how a good storyteller uses the voice (loud and soft, fast and slow), pauses, gestures, face, eye contact and audience participation, and picks the technique that fits a part of a story, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.COU.mastery: Tells a count noun (chair, chairs) from a non-count noun (water, advice), uses many and a few with count nouns and much and a little with non-count nouns, and does not write advices, informations or furnitures, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_NOUNS.PLU.mastery: Writes the plural of nouns with the usual -s or -es, -ies after a consonant and y (baby, babies), -ves (knife, knives), the irregular plurals (child, children; man, men; tooth, teeth) and the nouns that do not change (sheep), in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the part for the need
choose what the part tells you
ENGL.G7.READIN.T2_INTENSIVE_READING_CL.B.mastery: Says what the cover, title page, blurb, contents page, author's note and glossary tell the reader and which part to read first to decide on a book, and does not mix them up, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T2_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.E.mastery: Ends a statement with a full stop, a question with a question mark and a strong feeling or command with an exclamation mark, and does not use a question mark after a reported question, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the way to read for the task
ENGL.G7.READIN.T3_READING_INFORMATION_.I.mastery: Says that reading for information is to find facts (a timetable, a notice) and reading for meaning is to understand and enjoy what the writer says (a story, a poem), and chooses which to do for a task, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T3_VERBS_AND_TENSE.IRREGU.mastery: Writes the past form (went, saw, ate) and the past participle (gone, seen, eaten) of common irregular verbs, tells them from regular verbs that add -ed, and does not write goed, seen for saw or have went, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T3_VERBS_AND_TENSE.TENSE_.mastery: Uses the time word (every day, yesterday, next week) to choose the present, past or future form, and does not write yesterday I go or tomorrow I went, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T3_INTENSIVE_READING_PO.P.mastery: Counts the lines and the stanzas of a poem, finds the words that rhyme by sound (not spelling), the line or words that repeat (the refrain), and tells a poem from a story by its shape, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T3_WRITING_NARRATIVE_PA.N.mastery: Names the parts of a narrative paragraph (the opening that sets the scene, the events in order, the closing) and tells which sentence plays which part, and which does not belong, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T4_LISTENING_COMPREHENS.S.mastery: Says whether a question asks for the general idea or for a specific detail (a name, a number, a place, a time), and picks out the specific detail from a short text read to or by the learner, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the strategy for the purpose
ENGL.G7.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING.READ.mastery: Chooses skimming for a quick idea of a text, scanning for a name or number, predicting from the title and clues, and rereading with the words around a hard sentence, and names the strategy from what the reader does, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T4_VERBS_AND_TENSE.SIMPLE.mastery: Writes the simple present for habits and facts, adds -s or -es after he, she, it or one name (She walks, he washes), uses do not and does not with the plain verb, and does not write he walk or she do not know, in 8 of 10 new items.

Writes the simple past with -ed (with the spelling changes stopped, studied) or the irregular form, uses did not and did with the plain verb, and does not write did not went or she walkd, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_CL.C.mastery: Names the main character (the story is about the person) and a minor character (helps or gets in the way) from a short story, and says what the character does to move the story on, in 8 of 10 new items.

Chooses the trait that a character's words and actions support (brave, selfish, honest, jealous), and the line that is the evidence, and does not judge from the name or one word, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the clue that supports it
ENGL.G7.READIN.T4_INTENSIVE_READING_CL.P.mastery: Uses the title and the clues so far to choose the most likely next event and says which clue supports it, in 8 of 10 new passages.

forms: find the sentence that does not belong
ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T4_PARAGRAPHING_USING_E.P.mastery: Chooses the example or incident that supports the topic sentence, tells it from a sentence that is off the topic, and says which words introduce an example (for example, for instance), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T5_COMPARATIVE_AND_SUPE.A.mastery: Writes -er and -est for short adjectives, more and most for long ones, the irregular forms (good, better, best; bad, worse, worst), than with the comparative and the with the superlative, and does not write more taller or the most best, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T5_INTENSIVE_READING_OR.M.mastery: Says what makes a character a hero in a legend (brave, wise, generous), and chooses the moral lesson of a story, not a detail and not a lesson the story does not teach, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the part and its place
find the mistake in a letter
ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T5_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING_F.F.mastery: Puts the writer's address, date, greeting, body, closing (Your friend) and name in their places, and does not use the closing of a formal letter or write the receiver's address in a friendly letter, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T6_CONVERSATION_SKILLS.PO.mastery: Chooses the polite way to interrupt (Excuse me, may I say something?), to wait for a turn and to give one, tells it from a rude way, and says which gestures show politeness, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T6_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.A.mastery: Says whether an adverb tells when (yesterday, soon), where (here, outside) or how (slowly, carefully) an action happens, and does not name an adjective as an adverb, in 8 of 10 new items.

Writes the adverb of manner (quickly, well, hard), keeps the same form for fast, hard and late, does not write good for well or hardly for hard, and puts the adverb where it makes the meaning clear, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T6_COMMONLY_MISSPELT_WO.M.mastery: Spells words that often go wrong (because, friend, believe, beautiful, address, definitely, parliament, necessary, calendar, February) and picks the correct spelling from three that look alike, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the visual for the need
ENGL.G7.READIN.T7_INDEPENDENT_READING_.V.mastery: Says what kind of information a table, a bar graph, a pie chart, a map, a diagram and a timeline give, and reads a fact from a small table or chart, and does not read a row for a column, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T7_PERSONAL_AND_POSSESS.P.mastery: Uses the subject form (I, he, she, we, they) before a verb and the object form (me, him, her, us, them) after a verb or preposition, and does not write me and him went or between you and I, in 8 of 10 new items.

Tells a possessive adjective before a noun (my book) from a possessive pronoun that stands alone (the book is mine), writes its (belonging) and it's (it is) correctly, and does not write her's or your's, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: what is done at this step
ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T7_COMPOSITION_THE_WRIT.W.mastery: Names the steps (planning, drafting, revising, editing, publishing), says what is done at each and puts them in order, and does not edit before the draft is written, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T8_SIMPLE_PREPOSITIONS.PR.mastery: Says whether a preposition shows time (at, on, in), place (beside, under) or direction (to, into, across), chooses at, on or in for times and places, and does not write at Monday or in the morning of Friday, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T8_COMPOSITION_WRITING_.A.mastery: Says which part of a narrative to check for what (the introduction for who, where and when, the body for events in order, the conclusion for how it ends), and the first step of an assessment (reading it again slowly), and finds the part that needs work, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: pick the word with the same sound
ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T9_PRONUNCIATION_CONSON.S.mastery: Picks the word with the short sound of put (/ʊ/) or the long sound of food (/uː/), and does not match words by spelling (look and food both have oo), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T9_CONJUNCTIONS.CONJUNCTI.mastery: Uses and to add, but to show a difference and or to give a choice, and does not write but and or two joining words together, or a comma where and is needed, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T9_INTENSIVE_READING_CL.S.mastery: Puts four events of a story in the order they happened, using time words such as first, then, after and finally, in 8 of 10 new passages.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T9_CREATIVE_WRITING_NAR.N.mastery: Names the features of a narrative (a title, characters, a setting, a problem, events in order, a ending), tells a narrative from a description or a letter, and finds the part that is missing, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the part of a speech
ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T10_ORAL_PRESENTATIONS_D..mastery: Names the occasions for a speech (a wedding, a funeral, a school assembly, a prize day), the parts of a speech (greeting, introduction, body, conclusion, thanks) and the features of a good delivery, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T10_STUDY_SKILLS_NOTE_MA..mastery: Tells a main point from a supporting point, and chooses the notes that keep the main points in a few words (not whole sentences and not only a detail), in 8 of 10 new texts.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T10_DETERMINERS.ARTICLES.mastery: Chooses a before a consonant sound (a university), an before a vowel sound (an hour, an egg), and the for one named or known thing, and does not use a before a vowel sound or the before a general idea, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the list for the event
ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T10_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING_P..mastery: Puts items under the heading they belong to (food, clothes, tools, stationery), finds the item that does not belong in a group, and chooses the list that fits the event, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T11_INTERVIEWS.INTERVIEW_.mastery: Names why a person sits an interview (a school place, a scholarship, a job), chooses the confident and polite answer, asks for clarification politely (Could you repeat the question?), and spots a poor answer, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T11_FORMATION_OF_ADJECTI..mastery: Forms the adjective from a noun or verb with -ful, -less, -y, -ous, -al, -ive or -able (care, careful; danger, dangerous; create, creative), and keeps the spelling right (beauty, beautiful), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T11_INTENSIVE_READING_DI..mastery: Says that a dilemma narrative ends with a hard choice put to the listener (Who was right? What would you have done?), picks the closing question, and tells it from a narrative that ends with a lesson, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T11_SPELLING_ANTONYMS_SY..mastery: Chooses and writes a word with the same meaning (synonym) or the opposite meaning (antonym) in a sentence, spells it correctly, and does not give a word that is related but not the same, in 8 of 10 new items.
Spells numbers in words (fourteen, forty, ninety, eighth), writes ordinals with the right ending (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 21st) and puts the hyphen in twenty-one to ninety-nine, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T12_LISTENING_VIEWS_OPIN..mastery: Chooses the expression that shows a view (In my opinion, I believe, I feel that, As I see it), tells a view from a fact, and agrees or disagrees politely (I see your point, but ...), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T12_PHRASAL_VERBS.PHRASAL.mastery: Gives the meaning of put on, put off, put out, come across, come up with, give up, give in and give away from the sentence, and picks the right particle, not a word that only looks like it, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: find the mistake in a dialogue
ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T12_THE_WRITING_PROCESS_..mastery: Puts the speaker's name, a colon and the words spoken on a new line for each turn, writes actions in brackets, and does not use quotation marks round every line of a play-style dialogue, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T13_LISTENING_COMPREHENS..mastery: Chooses the right word (passenger, fare, route, junction, conductor, terminus, luggage, timetable, journey, destination) to complete a sentence about travel, and does not mix a person with a place or a thing, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T13_INTENSIVE_READING_CO..mastery: Chooses the sentence or title that covers the whole passage, tells it from a detail, and finds a specific detail asked for, in 8 of 10 new passages.

forms: choose what the summary leaves out
ENGL.G7.READIN.T13_INTENSIVE_READING_CO..mastery: Chooses the short account that has the key ideas in the right order, and does not choose one that is a single detail, a copy of the first lines or that adds something the passage does not say, in 8 of 10 new passages.

forms: choose the line that paints a picture
ENGL.G7.READIN.T13_INTENSIVE_READING_CO..mastery: Picks the words of a passage that make a picture, says what the writer wants the reader to see, hear or feel, and does not pick the line that only gives a fact, in 8 of 10 new passages.
Uses the words around an unfamiliar word to choose its meaning and says which words gave the clue, in 8 of 10 new passages.
Finds an answer that is stated in the passage, tells true from false and not stated, and does not pick a detail that sits near the answer, in 8 of 10 new passages.
Works out what the passage does not say outright (why a character acts, how a person feels) and does not give an answer the passage contradicts or merely repeats, in 8 of 10 new passages.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T13_SENTENCES_SIMPLE_SEN..mastery: Says that a simple sentence has one subject and one verb and tells a complete thought, tells it from a fragment that has no verb or no subject, and from two sentences joined without a joining word, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T13_ORAL_LITERATURE_PRAI..mastery: Says that a praise song honours a person (a chief, a runner, a bride) on an occasion, uses praise names and exaggeration, and tells the singer from the one praised, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: choose the idiom for the situation
ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T13_CREATIVE_WRITING_NAR..mastery: Gives the meaning of an idiom from its sentence (it is raining cats and dogs, spill the beans, a piece of cake, hit the nail on the head), and does not read it word for word, in 8 of 10 new items.

forms: pick the word with the same sound
ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T14_CONSONANT_SOUNDS_AND..mastery: Picks the word that starts or ends with the sound named, tells /f/ from /v/ (five, fiver) and /n/ from /ŋ/ (sin, sing), and does not match by spelling, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T14_SUBJECT_VERB_AGREEME..mastery: Finds the subject and the verb of a sentence, makes the verb agree with a singular or plural subject (The boys play, the boy plays), and does not let a noun near the verb decide the agreement (The box of mangoes is heavy), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T14_FEATURES_OF_STYLE.STY.mastery: Says that dialogue is the words characters speak, a simile compares with like or as and a metaphor says one thing is another, picks each from a short text, and completes a simile or a metaphor, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T14_DESCRIPTIVE_WRITING_..mastery: Names what makes writing descriptive (the five senses, adjectives and adverbs, similes, an order such as top to bottom), tells a description from a narrative, and picks the sentence with the best detail, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.LISTEN.T15_ORAL_REPORTS.ORAL_REP.mastery: Puts the parts of an oral report in order (greeting, what happened, who, when and where, the end), and picks the sentence that opens or closes a report, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T15_READING_FLUENCY.FLUEN.mastery: Names how a fluent reader reads (the right speed, a changing voice for feelings, a short pause at a comma and a longer one at a full stop, words read in groups, a text read again) and tells a fluent reader from one who reads flat, too fast or word by word, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.GRAMMA.T15_AFFIRMATIVE_AND_NEGA..mastery: Tells an affirmative sentence from a negative one, makes a sentence negative with do not, does not, did not, is not or cannot, and does not write a double negative (I do not have no pen), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.READIN.T15_POETRY.POEM_MEANING.mastery: Chooses the subject of a poem (what it is about), the message the poet wants to pass on, and the idea in a line, and does not choose a detail as the subject or an idea the poem does not hold, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G7.WRITIN.T15_FUNCTIONAL_WRITING_N..mastery: Names the parts of a notice (heading, what, when, where, who to see, the writer and the date) and of a poster (a big heading, a few words, a picture, the details), and finds the part that is missing, in 8 of 10 new items.
